newsitem.title: UK: Spice Girls' album reaches top of U.S. charts.
newsitem.headline: Spice Girls' album reaches top of U.S. charts.

text.p: The Spice Girls have reached the top of the U.S. pop charts with their first album, becoming the first British group in recent times to have conquered the United States with their debut release.

The Virgin record company said on Wednesday that the five- girl band, who have taken Britain and many other countries by storm since launching their first single less than a year ago, had reached the top of the American Billboard 200.
The charts are due to be officially released on Friday.
"It's fantastic. I can't remember the last time a British act sold this number of albums," a spokesman for Virgin told reporters.

The Spice Girls' first single record "Wannabe" reached the top of the U.S. charts last month after the group confounded critics who claimed they could not sing by performing live on American television.
The girls, who plan to make a feature film later this year, were due to appear on a leading U.S. chat show on Wednesday night.
Their success in the United States has outstripped that of British rock band Oasis who, like many other pop acts, have struggled to repeat there the success they have enjoyed in Europe.
Their achievement is however yet to match the 1960s dominance of the Beatles, who had 15 number one albums in the United States.
